newsitem.title: SPAIN: Acerinox outstrips after cash payback.
newsitem.headline: Acerinox outstrips after cash payback.

text.p: Shares in Spanish steel producer Acerinox bucked the bourse trend on Wednesday, shifting sharply higher after the firm announced a cut in the nominal value of shares and a cash payment to shareholders, dealers said.
At 1200 GMT, Acerinox was up 290 pesetas, 1.17 percent, to 25,150, off an earlier high of 25,890 pesetas. The Ibex-35 blue chip index meanwhile was down 1.43 percent to 6,579.69.
"The firm has excess cash, and its investment plans are covered, so this is a logical move to reward shareholders," said Javier Bernat, analyst at Inverban brokerage.
The steel producer said earlier that it would reduce the nominal value of its shares to 800 pesetas from 900 pesetas, paying back the difference to shareholders.
It would also return paid-in capital to shareholders, although a company spokesman declined to specify the amount.
"We think it's got further upside, and my (medium term) target is around 27,000 pesetas," Bernat said.
"It's the best pick in the European (steel) sector, and has shown itself to be very efficient during downtrends in the industrial cycle," he added.
Analysts said Acerinox has bright prospects on the basis of its operating efficiency. Furthermore steel prices are seen recovering.
Acerinox said earlier this month that its output and sales prospects were "excellent with a moderate stainless steel price uptrend" at least until the summer.
Plans to return cash to shareholders are to be approved at the next shareholders' meeting.
